summary: Iteration 4 end-to-end validation of French State B2C e-invoicing compliance features + scheduled background sync. Backend: 68/68 pytest passing (52 previous + 16 new in test_ereporting_invoice.py) covering settings legal fields (SIREN/SIRET/vat_regime/vat_rate) persistence, e-reporting JSON+CSV shape and aggregation (franchise: rate=0, ht==ttc, tva=0; assujetti 20%: ht=ttc/1.2, tva=ttc-ht), sequential idempotent invoice numbering (INV-YYYY-NNNNN), invoice 400 on unpaid, 403 on non-owner, and manual stock-sync endpoints. Frontend: admin Réglages tab renders all required data-testids (settings-legal, settings-legal-form, settings-siren, settings-siret, ereporting-export-btn, settings-save-btn); values (SASU / 123456789 / 12345678900001) persisted across page reload; ereporting-export-btn triggered download of ereporting-B2C-2026-07-26.csv. Background loops verified: no *sync loop error* in backend logs, stock sync-all completed successfully (15 products), _stock_sync_loop + _tracking_sync_loop created at startup and gated by STOCK_AUTO_SYNC/CJ_AUTO_SYNC env (default true).
action_items: OPTIONAL: When paying assujetti VAT test, e-reporting JSON returns vat_rate=20.0 (float). CSV writes '20' via format `{vat_rate:.0f}` — this rounds e.g. 5.5% to '6' in CSV. If reduced/intermediate rates (5.5, 10, 20) are ever supported, switch CSV to `%.2f` or `%g` and revisit the SettingsInput vat_rate default (currently 20.0).

OPTIONAL: /api/settings is a fully public endpoint (extras.py L58) and exposes SIREN/SIRET/vat_number to anonymous users. These are actually public data in France (Kbis) so it's OK, but if any Admin ever stores an EMAIL/PHONE there it will leak. Consider splitting into /settings (public: banner, whatsapp, company_name) and /settings/legal (admin-only, or public but curated).

OPTIONAL: Invoice counter uses one counter per YEAR (`counters._id = invoice-{year}`) which is correct — but there is no unique index on `orders.invoice_number`. If two concurrent GET /orders/{id}/invoice calls hit the same order simultaneously they could both call find_one_and_update on the counter before the order's invoice_number is set, granting the SAME order two sequential numbers and wasting one. Add a unique sparse index on orders.invoice_number OR wrap _next_invoice_number in an application-level lock keyed by order_id.

OPTIONAL: Background loops have no way to be observed at runtime (no /admin/health showing 'last stock sync at' / 'last tracking sync at'). Suggest exposing `last_stock_sync_at` and `last_tracking_sync_at` on GET /api/admin/analytics or a new /api/admin/health-sync endpoint for the SRE dashboard.
critical_code_review_comments: ops.py L403 CSV writes vat_rate with `{vat_rate:.0f}` which truncates fractional rates (5.5 → '6'). Use `{vat_rate:g}` or `{vat_rate:.2f}` if reduced-rate VAT (5.5, 10) is ever used.

ops.py `_next_invoice_number` has a race window between `counters.find_one_and_update` (increment) and `orders.update_one` (set invoice_number). Two concurrent requests for the same paid order can both increment the counter before either persists the number on the order — the second call would then see order.invoice_number set and skip the increment, but the first call's number gets discarded. Impact is a gap in the invoice sequence (regulatory compliance requires CONTINUOUS numbering per art. 289 CGI). Recommend: use `orders.find_one_and_update({id, invoice_number: {$exists: false}}, ...)` pattern, or wrap in per-order asyncio.Lock, or add unique index on invoice_number and retry on duplicate.

extras.py — DEFAULT_SETTINGS has `vat_regime='franchise'` and `vat_rate=20.0`. When regime is franchise, vat_rate is ignored (ops.py L242 uses 0.0), which is correct. But the field is still returned publicly in /api/settings, potentially confusing external readers. Consider not returning vat_rate when regime=='franchise'.

server.py L921-924 — asyncio.create_task references are not stored anywhere. If the coroutine raises and returns, Python may log 'Task was destroyed but it is pending' warnings and there's no way to restart or observe. Consider storing app.state.background_tasks = [asyncio.create_task(...)] and adding a shutdown handler to cancel them cleanly.
ops.py `ereporting` loads up to 50000 orders into memory (L384). Fine for MVP but should switch to a Mongo `$group` pipeline (by {$dateToString: '%Y-%m-%d'}, rate) once orders grow past ~10k paid.

Frontend Admin.jsx `exportEreporting` L673 hard-codes days=90. Consider surfacing a date-range picker (or 30/90/365 selector) in Réglages — as-is, admin cannot export a single-month CSV for URSSAF submissions.

seed_data_creation: Ephemeral orders are created and DELETED at test-teardown time via _mdb.orders.delete_many. Aggregation tests may briefly add up to 2 paid orders on days -1/-2 and 1 on day -15, all cleaned up. Settings were toggled to assujetti during one test and restored to franchise at end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full backend regression: `pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v` — 68 tests in ~15s, all green. New test file: /app/backend/tests/test_ereporting_invoice.py. Key gotchas kept from iteration 3 still apply: (1) NO admin API to flip payment_status — use pymongo direct write via /app/backend/.env MONGO_URL+DB_NAME (helper _create_paid_order does this). (2) POST /api/orders requires shipping_address.email (Pydantic 422 otherwise) — this bit me in first run. (3) Invoice numbers are per-YEAR sequential starting at INV-2026-00001; two calls on the same order return the same number (idempotent), two different paid orders get seq N and N+1. (4) e-reporting JSON: keys are regime/vat_rate/period_days/operation_type/totals/rows; CSV first line 'date;taux_tva;nb_operations;total_ht;total_tva;total_ttc;devise;type'. (5) Background loops: `_stock_sync_loop` waits 300s before first run, `_tracking_sync_loop` waits 120s — so during a short test window you may not see the loop firing; the manual endpoints POST /admin/products/{id}/sync-stock and POST /admin/products/sync-stock-all are what the loops call. (6) CJ API occasional 429 — test_sync_single_admin_ok tolerates (200, 429). (7) TEST banner FR is still set in DB from iterations 2/3 — visible in storefront hero banner, non-blocking. (8) The one flaky spot to watch: if e-reporting aggregation tests run concurrently with each other via pytest-xdist and both switch vat_regime, they could stomp. Currently only test_aggregation_assujetti_20pct changes regime and restores at the end; test_aggregation_franchise resets first. Both are in the same file and pytest-xdist LoadScopeScheduling groups them together — safe.
rca of the issue: No blocking issues found. One minor test-authoring miss on my first run: /api/orders now requires shipping_address.email (Pydantic v2 model). Added `email: CUSTOMER_EMAIL` in the two _create_paid_order helper payloads and unpaid test payload → all 16 tests green on 2nd run. Root cause of the schema change is unrelated to this iteration — model was updated in a prior iteration but the test scaffolding lagged.
